_note: Curated summaries of Indian law for Praja Raksha. Plain-language summaries written for awareness, not legal advice. Verify with the official Bare Acts (indiacode.nic.in) before relying on them.

sections.title: Assault or criminal force on a woman with intent to outrage her modesty
sections.summary: Using force or assaulting a woman intending to outrage her modesty.
sections.punishment: 1 to 5 years imprisonment and fine

sections.title: Sexual harassment
sections.summary: Unwelcome physical contact or advances, demanding sexual favours, showing pornography against her will, or making sexually coloured remarks to a woman.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years and/or fine (up to 1 year for sexually coloured remarks)

sections.title: Assault or criminal force with intent to disrobe a woman
sections.summary: Assaulting or using force on a woman intending to disrobe her or compel her to be naked.
sections.punishment: 3 to 7 years imprisonment and fine

sections.title: Voyeurism
sections.summary: Watching or capturing images of a woman in a private act where she expects privacy, or sharing such images.
sections.punishment: 1 to 3 years and fine (first conviction); 3 to 7 years on repeat

sections.title: Stalking
sections.summary: Repeatedly following or contacting a woman despite clear disinterest, or monitoring her use of the internet, email or electronic communication.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years and fine (first conviction); up to 5 years on repeat

sections.title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman
sections.summary: Words, sounds, gestures or objects intended to insult a woman's modesty, or intruding on her privacy.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years and fine

sections.title: Dowry death
sections.summary: Death of a woman by burns, injury or unnatural circumstances within 7 years of marriage, where she faced cruelty or harassment for dowry before death.
sections.punishment: 7 years to life imprisonment

sections.title: Cruelty by husband or his relatives
sections.summary: Husband or his relatives subjecting a woman to cruelty: conduct likely to drive her to suicide or cause grave injury, or harassment to meet unlawful demands such as dowry.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years and fine

sections.title: Voluntarily causing hurt
sections.summary: Intentionally causing bodily pain, disease or infirmity to a person.
sections.punishment: Up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs 10,000, or both

sections.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
sections.summary: Intentionally causing serious injury such as fractures, permanent disfigurement or loss of sight or hearing.
sections.punishment: Up to 7 years and fine

sections.title: Wrongful restraint
sections.summary: Obstructing a person from going where they have a right to go.
sections.punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both

sections.title: Wrongful confinement
sections.summary: Restraining a person so they cannot leave certain limits, such as locking someone in a room.
sections.punishment: Up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both (higher for longer confinement)

sections.title: Theft
sections.summary: Dishonestly taking movable property out of someone's possession without consent.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine, or both

sections.title: Extortion
sections.summary: Putting a person in fear of injury to make them hand over money, property or valuables, including threatening to leak photos unless paid.
sections.punishment: Up to 7 years, or fine, or both

sections.title: Criminal breach of trust
sections.summary: Dishonestly misusing or keeping property or money that was entrusted to you.
sections.punishment: Up to 5 years, or fine, or both

sections.title: Cheating
sections.summary: Deceiving someone to dishonestly make them hand over money or property.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years (basic); up to 7 years and fine when property is delivered through cheating

sections.title: Cheating by personation
sections.summary: Cheating by pretending to be another person.
sections.punishment: Up to 5 years, or fine, or both

sections.title: Criminal trespass and house-trespass
sections.summary: Entering someone's property or house unlawfully to commit an offence, intimidate, insult or annoy.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 months or fine up to Rs 5,000 (trespass); up to 1 year or fine up to Rs 5,000 (house-trespass)

sections.title: Criminal intimidation
sections.summary: Threatening injury to a person, their reputation or property to cause alarm or force them to act.
sections.punishment: Up to 2 years and/or fine; up to 7 years if the threat is of death or grievous hurt

sections.title: Intentional insult to provoke breach of peace
sections.summary: Intentionally insulting a person, knowing it is likely to provoke them to break public peace.
sections.punishment: Up to 2 years, or fine, or both

sections.title: Defamation
sections.summary: Making or publishing false statements, including online, that harm a person's reputation.
sections.punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both, or community service

sections.title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR, Zero FIR, e-FIR)
sections.summary: Police must register an FIR for a cognizable offence. It can be filed at any police station irrespective of where the offence happened (Zero FIR), and can be given electronically (e-FIR). If the officer refuses, the complainant can send the complaint to the Superintendent of Police (Section 173(4)).
sections.punishment: Procedural right, not an offence

sections.title: Magistrate can order investigation
sections.summary: If police and the SP do not act, a Magistrate can order police to investigate on an application by the complainant.
sections.punishment: Procedural right, not an offence

sections.title: Identity theft
sections.summary: Fraudulently using someone else's password, electronic signature or other unique identification.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years and fine up to Rs 1 lakh

sections.title: Cheating by personation using a computer resource
sections.summary: Cheating someone online by pretending to be another person, such as fake profiles, fake bank officials or fake police calls.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years and fine up to Rs 1 lakh

sections.title: Violation of privacy
sections.summary: Capturing, publishing or transmitting images of a person's private area without consent.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine up to Rs 2 lakh, or both

sections.title: Publishing or transmitting obscene material electronically
sections.summary: Publishing or sending obscene content online.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years and fine up to Rs 5 lakh (first conviction)

sections.title: Publishing or transmitting sexually explicit material electronically
sections.summary: Publishing or sending sexually explicit content online, such as leaking intimate videos.
sections.punishment: Up to 5 years and fine up to Rs 10 lakh (first conviction)

sections.title: Sexually explicit material depicting children
sections.summary: Publishing, sending, browsing or creating sexually explicit material involving children.
sections.punishment: Up to 5 years and fine up to Rs 10 lakh (first conviction)

sections.law: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
sections.title: Application to Magistrate for relief
sections.summary: A woman facing domestic violence (physical, sexual, verbal, emotional or economic) can apply to a Magistrate, directly or through a Protection Officer, for relief.
sections.punishment: Civil remedy

sections.law: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
sections.title: Protection orders
sections.summary: Magistrate can order the abuser to stop violence, not contact her, and not enter her workplace.
sections.punishment: Breach of a protection order is punishable under Section 31 (up to 1 year and/or fine up to Rs 20,000)

sections.law: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
sections.title: Residence orders
sections.summary: Woman cannot be thrown out of the shared household; the Magistrate can protect her right to live there.
sections.punishment: Civil remedy

sections.law: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
sections.title: Monetary relief
sections.summary: Magistrate can order the abuser to pay for losses, medical expenses and maintenance.
sections.punishment: Civil remedy

sections.title: Giving, taking or demanding dowry
sections.summary: Giving or taking dowry (Section 3) and demanding dowry (Section 4) are offences.
sections.punishment: Section 3: at least 5 years and fine; Section 4: 6 months to 2 years and fine

sections.law: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013
sections.title: Complaint to Internal Committee
sections.summary: A woman facing sexual harassment at work can complain in writing to the Internal Committee (or Local Committee) within 3 months of the incident.
sections.punishment: Inquiry can lead to action against the harasser

sections.law: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
sections.title: Sexual offences against children
sections.summary: Covers sexual assault and harassment of anyone under 18. Anyone who knows of such an offence must report it to police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit (Section 19).
sections.punishment: Severe, depending on the offence

sections.title: Atrocities against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
sections.summary: Insulting, intimidating, abusing by caste name in public view, or other atrocities against SC/ST members.
sections.punishment: 6 months to 5 years and fine for most offences (higher for serious ones)

sections.title: Consumer complaint to District Commission
sections.summary: A consumer cheated by a defective product, deficient service or unfair trade practice can file a complaint with the District Consumer Commission, also online via e-Daakhil.
sections.punishment: Compensation, refund or replacement
